title: Achyranthes Bidentata Radix mitigates neuronal apoptosis via regulation of JUN and CREB in the cAMP signaling pathway.
authors: Liu, Yan; Chang, Ai-Bing; Liu, Yan-Ru; Tang, Zhi-Shu; Song, Zhong-Xing; Fan, Xiu-He; Zhou, Mi; Wang, Xing-Chi
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药牛膝通过JUN/CREB-cAMP通路抗神经元凋亡，虽含分子对接和动力学模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白靶点而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although Achyranthes Bidentata Radix (ABR) demonstrates neuroprotective potential in NDDs, its anti-apoptotic mechanisms remain unclear. PURPOSE: To decipher ABR's key bioactive compounds and their regulation of neuronal apoptosis via the JUN/CREB-cAMP axis. METHODS: An integrated discovery-validation strategy synergized LC-MS characterization, multi-omics analysis, computational modeling and qRT-PCR technologies were carried to identify and validate ABR's key bioactive compounds and apoptosis targets through zebrafish for in vivo verification and HT22 cells for in vitro mechanistic analysis. RESULTS: UPLC-MS/MS profiling integrated with ADME screening and network topology analysis identified beta-Ecdysone, Quercetin, 25R-inokosterone, and 25S-inokosterone as ABR's key active compounds targeting JUN/CREB. Initial in vivo and in vitro studies demonstrated ABR's has neuroprotection in AlCl(3)-induced models in a dose-depended manner. Integrated metabolomic-transcriptomic mapping of zebrafish models revealed cAMP signaling biomarkers including cAMP, AMP, and dopamine, establishing JUN and CREB as key therapeutic targets. Machine learning modeling with 11 algorithms further prioritized JUN/CREB for neuronal apoptosis risk prediction, while molecular docking and dynamics simulations characterized stable compound-target interactions. Ultimately, qRT-PCR validation confirmed ABR's dose-dependent modulation of JUN and CREB, thus mechanistically anchoring the neuroprotective effects. CONCLUSION: ABR facilitates neuroprotection through bioactive compound-driven regulation of the JUN/CREB-cAMP axis, providing a mechanistic framework for NDDs therapy.
abstract_zh: 背景：尽管牛膝 (Achyranthes Bidentata Radix, ABR) 在神经退行性疾病 (NDDs) 中显示出神经保护潜力，但其抗凋亡机制仍不清楚。目的：阐明ABR的关键生物活性化合物及其通过JUN/CREB-cAMP轴调控神经元凋亡的作用。方法：采用整合发现-验证策略，结合LC-MS表征、多组学分析、计算建模和qRT-PCR技术，通过斑马鱼进行体内验证和HT22细胞进行体外机制分析，以识别并验证ABR的关键生物活性化合物及凋亡靶点。结果：UPLC-MS/MS分析结合ADME筛选和网络拓扑分析，鉴定出beta-蜕皮甾酮 (beta-Ecdysone)、槲皮素 (Quercetin)、25R-牛膝甾酮 (25R-inokosterone) 和25S-牛膝甾酮 (25S-inokosterone) 为ABR靶向JUN/CREB的关键活性化合物。初步体内和体外研究表明，ABR在AlCl(3)诱导模型中呈剂量依赖性神经保护作用。斑马鱼模型的整合代谢组-转录组图谱揭示了cAMP信号生物标志物，包括cAMP、AMP和多巴胺，确立JUN和CREB为关键治疗靶点。基于11种算法的机器学习建模进一步优先选择JUN/CREB用于神经元凋亡风险预测，而分子对接和动力学模拟表征了稳定的化合物-靶点相互作用。最终，qRT-PCR验证确认了ABR对JUN和CREB的剂量依赖性调节，从而在机制上锚定了神经保护效应。结论：ABR通过生物活性化合物驱动的JUN/CREB-cAMP轴调控促进神经保护，为NDDs治疗提供了机制框架。
